chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'The most superior of the deeds in the Presence of God is what is performed by (following) the Sunnah, even though it may be little.'

key_terms.أَفْضَلَ الْأَعْمَالِ: The most superior of deeds — ranked by their conformity to the Sunnah, not their outward magnitude
key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: The Sunnah — the established practice and tradition of the Prophet (SAWW), the normative model of Islamic conduct

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sajjad say is the best deed in the sight of God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sajjad (peace be upon him), the fourth Imam, taught that quality of religious action matters more than quantity — a small deed done in conformity with the established Sunnah of the Prophet surpasses larger deeds that deviate from it. This teaching addressed those who might prioritize seemingly impressive but ungrounded religious acts over consistent adherence to prophetic practice. For the early Muslim community, following the Sunnah was not merely imitation but a spiritual discipline of alignment with the Prophet's lived example, and this hadith emphasizes that even modest deeds performed in that spirit are superior to elaborate ones divorced from it.
